name: Prince Edward Island
tagline: Canada's smallest province, red sand beaches and rolling farmland moving at a pace the mainland genuinely forgot.
highlight: Walking a red sand beach at low tide, the cliffs behind glowing rust-orange in the evening light exactly as they do in the books that made this island famous.
shortDescription: Canada's smallest province, home to the red sand beaches and farmland that inspired Anne of Green Gables, plus some of the country's best seafood.
metaDescription: A Prince Edward Island travel guide: Green Gables, PEI National Park's red beaches, Charlottetown, lobster suppers, food and how to plan a visit.
knownFor: Green Gables, red sand beaches, PEI lobster suppers

image.alt: Red sand cliffs at Prince Edward Island National Park

intro: Prince Edward Island is genuinely Canada's smallest province, a gentle landscape of red sand beaches, rolling farmland and small fishing harbours that feels a world away from the Rockies or big city life.
It's genuinely also the setting for Anne of Green Gables, the beloved novel that still draws visitors to the farmhouse and landscape that inspired it.
The island's real character genuinely comes through in its seafood — lobster suppers, fresh mussels and PEI's own celebrated potatoes fill menus across the province.

whyVisit.intro: Prince Edward Island's case rests genuinely on a slower pace and a landscape unlike anywhere else in Canada.

points.title: The red sand beaches are genuinely striking
points.text: Iron-rich soil gives the island's coastline a distinctive rust-red colour found almost nowhere else.

points.title: Green Gables is genuinely a real literary pilgrimage
points.text: The farmhouse and landscape that inspired one of Canada's most beloved novels.

points.title: The seafood is genuinely some of the best in Canada
points.text: Lobster, mussels and oysters landed fresh from the surrounding waters.

points.title: The pace here is genuinely deliberately slower
points.text: Small towns, farm stands and a real absence of big-city hurry.

points.title: It works genuinely well as a distinctive add-on trip
points.text: A very different side of Canada from the mountains or big cities.

attractionsIntro: Prince Edward Island's essential sights are genuinely spread between its literary landmarks and its red sand coastline.

attractions.name: Green Gables Heritage Place

image.alt: Green Gables Heritage Place in Prince Edward Island

attractions.text: Genuinely the farmhouse that inspired Anne of Green Gables, restored and furnished as it appears in the novel.
attractions.tip: Genuinely walk the surrounding Haunted Wood and Lovers' Lane trails for the full literary setting.

attractions.name: Prince Edward Island National Park's red beaches

image.alt: Red sand cliffs at Prince Edward Island National Park

attractions.text: Genuinely the island's most striking natural feature, sandstone cliffs and dunes coloured rust-red by iron in the soil.
attractions.tip: Genuinely visit at low tide for the widest, most walkable stretch of beach.

attractions.name: The Confederation Bridge

image.alt: The Confederation Bridge connecting PEI to the mainland

attractions.text: Genuinely one of the world's longest bridges over ice-covered water, connecting the island to mainland New Brunswick.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a striking 13-kilometre drive in itself, best appreciated slowly rather than rushed.

attractions.name: Charlottetown's historic streets

image.alt: Charlottetown's historic streets in Prince Edward Island

attractions.text: Genuinely the birthplace of Canadian Confederation, its compact downtown lined with well-preserved Victorian buildings.
attractions.tip: Genuinely visit Province House, where the Confederation talks were first held, if it's open for tours.

attractions.name: Point Prim Lighthouse

image.alt: Point Prim Lighthouse in Prince Edward Island

attractions.text: Genuinely the island's oldest lighthouse, a distinctive round brick tower on a quiet, scenic point.
attractions.tip: Genuinely climb to the top if it's open — the coastal view is worth the narrow stairs.

attractions.name: The old wharf at PEI National Park

image.file: File:Old Wharf Posts on beach in Prince Edward Island National Park.jpg
image.alt: Old wharf posts on the beach at Prince Edward Island National Park

attractions.text: Genuinely an atmospheric, photogenic remnant, weathered wooden posts rising from the sand at low tide.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a rewarding subject for photography, especially at sunrise or sunset.

attractions.name: Green Gables' surrounding farmland

image.alt: The farmland behind Green Gables Heritage Place

attractions.text: Genuinely as much a part of the site as the house itself, gardens and fields evoking the novel's rural setting.
attractions.tip: Genuinely allow time to walk the grounds, not just tour the house interior.

thingsToDoIntro: Prince Edward Island genuinely rewards a slow pace, built around its beaches, small towns and seafood.

thingsToDo.title: Tour Green Gables Heritage Place
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential literary pilgrimage, walking through the rooms and grounds that inspired Anne of Green Gables.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely read or revisit the novel beforehand for the fullest appreciation of the site.

thingsToDo.title: Walk the red sand beaches of PEI National Park

image.alt: Walking the red sand beaches of PEI National Park

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential island experience, exploring dunes and cliffs found almost nowhere else in the world.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely bring water shoes if you plan to wade — the sandstone underfoot can be sharp in places.

thingsToDo.title: Drive across the Confederation Bridge
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely memorable arrival or departure, a long, curving drive suspended above the strait.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely a toll applies only when leaving the island, not arriving.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Charlottetown's waterfront

image.alt: Charlottetown's waterfront in Prince Edward Island

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely relaxed way to spend an afternoon, browsing shops and restaurants along the historic harbour.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely check the events calendar — the waterfront often hosts markets and live music in summer.

thingsToDo.title: Visit Point Prim Lighthouse
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely peaceful stop, a scenic drive to the island's oldest lighthouse on a quiet coastal point.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely combine with a stop at a nearby oyster shack — the area is known for its seafood.

thingsToDo.title: Eat a traditional PEI lobster supper
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential island tradition, a full lobster meal served family-style, often in a church hall or community setting.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely book ahead in peak summer — the island's most famous lobster suppers do fill up.

options.text: Genuinely the standard route from mainland New Brunswick.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Prince Edward Island visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Rent genuinely a car — public transport is limited outside Charlottetown.
Book genuinely a lobster supper ahead in peak summer season.
Visit genuinely outside summer only if you've confirmed your planned attractions stay open.
Pack genuinely water shoes for exploring the red sandstone beaches.
Time genuinely your Confederation Bridge crossing — the toll only applies when leaving the island.
Try genuinely both mussels and lobster — the island's two signature seafood dishes.

faq.q: How many days do you need on Prince Edward Island?
faq.a: Three to four days genuinely covers Green Gables, the red sand coastline and Charlottetown at a relaxed pace.

faq.q: Is Prince Edward Island worth visiting?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — its red sand beaches, literary history and seafood offer a distinctive, slower-paced side of Canada.

faq.q: Do you need a car on PEI?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — public transport is limited, and a car is the practical way to reach beaches, lighthouses and small towns.

faq.q: How do you get to Prince Edward Island?
faq.a: Genuinely by car across the Confederation Bridge, seasonal ferry from Nova Scotia, or direct flight to Charlottetown.

faq.q: Is Green Gables worth visiting if you haven't read the book?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely, though reading or revisiting Anne of Green Gables beforehand genuinely deepens the experience.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit PEI?
faq.a: Genuinely June through September, when beaches, restaurants and lobster suppers are all fully open.
